newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bausch to market Pharmos drug.
newsitem.headline: Bausch to market Pharmos drug.

text.p: Pharmos Corp said on Sunday that Bausch & Lomb has agreed to market some of its ophthalmic drugs outside the United States and to make a $2 million investment in the company.

The agreement grants Bausch the right to market Pharmos' Lotemax product line, which includes an ophthalmic steroid, an allergy product and an antibiotic, outside the United States. Bausch also agreed to $1.6 million in milestone payments tied to regulatory approvals.

Pharmos, a Florida-based company that conducts most of its operations in Israel, said it had completed phase III studies of Lotemax and would be filing an amended new-drug application for it with the U.S. Food and Drug Adminstration in early 1997.
The marketing agreement follows a similar one between the two companies covering the U.S. market signed in June 1995.
In a separate agreement, Bausch purchased $2 million of common stock in Pharmos. Pharmos develps and commercializes treatments for ophthalmic and neurological disorders.
